title: 9-round AES-256: reported whole-key related-key partial sums, data conflict

display.name: Related-key partial sums, data conflict, full-key headline

target.description: The authors' reported whole-key attack on 9-round AES-256, with initial whitening and final MixColumns omitted. The detailed filter stage is separately recorded as aes256-9r-integral-fklssww2001-related-key-partial-sums-conflict; its selected subkey material and the broader whole-cipher claim have different scopes.

setting.key_relation: For an unknown base master key L, L_a XOR L has byte a at zero-based master-key byte indices 21 and 25 and zero elsewhere, for every a in 0,...,255. The a=0 key is the base key; total distinct keys is 256.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no weak-key restriction reported
setting.plaintext_model: About 32 structures, each containing 2^64 chosen plaintexts under each of 256 related master keys. Body total 2^77 conflicts with Table 1's 2^85.
assumptions: Wrong-subkey rejection uses the paper's heuristic model for zero XOR sums; no numerical whole-procedure success rate is supplied.
Related master keys use a fixed XOR relation, while their expanded-key differences depend on guessed base-key bytes through S-boxes. These are not arbitrary independently selectable subkey oracles.

This record retains the paper's explicit whole-cipher attack headline. The detailed search first isolates selected subkey material; repeated filtering, reverse expansion or residual search for full master-key completion is not separately costed for every endpoint in this version.

time.note: Section 4.3 gives 5*2^224 for five dominating structures, each scanning 2^72 ciphertexts for 2^152 outer guesses. Section 4.5 abbreviates this to 2^224 steps. The coefficient five is preserved; the dominant one-round-decryption workload is not silently converted to full AES encryptions. This whole-key row preserves the authors' attack-level estimate; it does not infer a new constant factor from the separately catalogued filter.

data.note: Both versions print the discrepancy. The body counts 32*(2^64*256)=2^77 total queries; Table 1 states 2^85. The table's extra factor 256 cannot be explained as a per-key/total conversion of the same stated structure count. The acquisition budget is the paper's reported attack-level budget.

memory.note: Neither the basic nor improved related-key construction provides an explicit complete peak-storage budget.

preprocessing.note: Table preparation and setup are described within the construction but not separately priced for this endpoint.

success.description: No numerical success for this exact key_recovery output is given. Section4.2 says enough sets identify the correct guesses; Section4.3 says about32 structures, without a joint error probability. The source 256-key relation and required plaintext compensation are conditions of the balanced identity. The existing Table1 2^85 versus body 2^77 data conflict remains pending; neither endpoint is silently selected. This is an author full-key headline; numerical success of unitemized completion is not inferred from the selected-subkey relation.

review.scope: Re-read PDF3-5 and11-16 Sections2.1-2.4/4.1-4.5. The improved related-key procedure intends unique guessed-byte output after about32 structures, but supplies no joint wrong-key law for these aggregate structures or explicit master-key completion for the headline. Earlier ordinary Square255/256 rejection is not that law. Retain partial/full separation, balanced-sum component and2^85-versus2^77 data conflict; both primary metrics remain unquantified.
